extraction.name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
extraction.description: A dataset containing 7,787 natural, grade-school science questions partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set, designed to encourage AI research in advanced question answering.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset consists of science questions drawn from a variety of sources, and a corpus created by running search queries relevant to science on a major search engine.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions authored for use on standardized tests and science-related sentences mined from the Web.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Documents were collected, de-duplicated, stripped of non-text content, and chunked into sentences.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: To encourage AI research in advanced question answering.

name.evidence: Together, these constitute the AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC), which requires far more powerful knowledge and reasoning than previous challenges such as SQuAD or SNLI.

description.evidence: The ARC question set is partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set... The dataset contains only natural, grade-school science questions (authored for human tests), and is the largest public-domain set of this kind (7,787 questions).

url.evidence: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, Models, and Leaderboard can be accessed at http://data.allenai.org/arc.

creator.evidence: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Seattle, WA, U.S.A.

publisher.evidence: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Seattle, WA, U.S.A.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The ARC dataset consists of 7787 science questions, all non-diagram, multiple choice (typically 4-way multiple choice). They are drawn from a variety of sources... The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The ARC Dataset consists of a collection of 7787 natural science questions , namely questions authored for use on standardized tests.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The top several documents from each search were collected and de-duplicated, and then the content of these documents was stripped down to capture just the text in each document. The resulting text was then chunked into sentences.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present a new question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering.
